SMT BINDU O V, PP  THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 25.09.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 193 of 2016  2025:KER:72168  3  ORDER (Dated this the 25th day of September, 2025)

The challenge in this revision petition is the conviction and sentence rendered against the revision petitioners under Sections 406 and 498A r/w 34 of IPC.
2.
The revision petitioners are accused Nos.1 and 2 respectively in CC No. 221/2002 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court I, Parappanangadi.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court I, Parappanangadi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
They, along with another accused stood trial before that court for committing the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 r/w 34 of IPC.
3.
The prosecution case in brief is as follows; The 1st accused married PW1 on 14.03.2002.

Thereafter, while living together in the house of the accused, the accused three in number, in furtherance of their common intention, misappropriated Rs.50,000/- and 40 sovereigns of gold ornaments out of the 50 sovereigns of gold ornaments given to PW1 at the time of the marriage.
It is also alleged that, the accused subjected PW1 to cruelty demanding more gold and money as dowry.
The trial court on an elaborate appreciation of the evidence on record found the 3 rd accused not guilty of the offences alleged and acquitted her.
But it found the 1 st accused guilty of committing an offence punishable under Section 406 IPC and accused Nos. 1 and 2 guilty of committing the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w 34 IPC.
Accordingly, it sentenced the 1st accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year under Section 406 IPC.

It also sentenced the 1st accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 1  years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-
under Section 498A, IPC with a default clause and the 2nd accused to undergo simple imprisonment Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025

5. Accused Nos. 1 and 2 carried the matter in appeal by filing Crl.Appeal No.369/2010 before the Sessions Court, Manjeri.
The said court by judgment dated 30.07.2015 dismissed the appeal.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioners and the learned public prosecutor.
7.

The learned counsel for the revision petitioners submitted that both the trial court and the appellate court have not appreciated the evidence in a proper perspective 2025:KER:72168 and has arrived at a wrong conclusion of guilt against the accused.

He contended that the evidence of PW1 and PW2 regarding the events are mired with contradictions and there is no credible evidence to prove the factum of misappropriation, as alleged by the prosecution.
He also argued that the evidence of PW1 would go to show that she is not having a consistent version regarding the events and that the medical evidence adduced does not support the prosecution case.
8. Per contra, the learned public prosecutor supported the impugned judgments and contended that there are no grounds to interfere with the same.

9. On going through the materials on record, it is seen that the 1st accused, the husband of PW1 has been convicted under Section 406 IPC on the ground that he has misappropriated Rs.50,000/- and 40 sovereigns of gold ornaments from out of the 50 sovereigns given to PW1 at the time of marriage.

PW1 the victim and PW2 her brother stated that the 1st accused has thus taken away the gold ornaments belonging to PW1 on different occasions by making PW1 believe that the money thus obtained by selling the ornaments will be used for the construction of a 2025:KER:72168 residential house.
It is to be taken note that as regards this allegation, the only evidence available is that of PW1 and evidence of PW2 on this aspect is nothing, but hearsay.
Further, the evidence of PW1 does not show as to when and how much quantity of gold ornaments, the 1 st accused has thus taken away from her and where it was sold.
In other words, the evidence of PW1 regarding the events of alleged misappropriation of gold is very vague, sans details.
The prosecution has also not adduced any evidence to show where these gold ornaments have been sold, its quantity and the amount allegedly received by the 1 st accused on such sale.

At this juncture, I will also take note of another relevant fact, ie; the prosecution has not adduced any convincing evidence to show that at the time of marriage, PW1 was given Rs.50,000/- and 50 sovereigns of gold ornaments as alleged.
Apart from the interested testimonies of PW1 and PW2, there is no convincing evidence on this aspect.
Even though the case of the prosecution is that the gold ornaments were purchased from a particular jewellery, not a scrap of paper has been produced to prove the same.
Further, the prosecution also did not choose to produce at least, the marriage photographs or examine anyone who had 2025:KER:72168 attended the marriage to substantiate its contentions.
In the light of the evidence as discussed above, I am of the view that the conviction of the 1 st accused under Section 406 IPC cannot be sustained.

10. Coming to the offence under Section 498A IPC, it is the prosecution case that the 1 st and 2nd accused have persistently demanded PW1 and PW2 to bring 25 sovereigns of gold ornaments and Rs.50,000/-, apart from the share in the property of the father of PW1 for the construction of the Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95767305/
3 house.

sentences.text: It is their case that, the 1st and 2nd accused have physically and mentally harassed PW1 for this purpose.
The prosecution is mainly relying upon the evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the evidence of PW5, coupled with Ext.P4 document to prove this fact.

The evidence of PW1 shows that even though she has jumbled the dates on which the events took place, has specifically deposed regarding the fact that she had called her brother(PW2), when a demand was thus made from the side of accused Nos. 1 and 2.
Then PW2 came to the house of PW1 and assured the 1 st and 2nd accused that he will try to procure the money within a month.
Thereafter, on 23.10.2001, PW2 came to the house of PW1 and informed the accused regarding his inability to procure 2025:KER:72168 the money as promised.
It is at this point of time, PW1 was physically and mentally harassed by A1 and A2 demanding money and gold.
On these aspect, it is to be seen that, the evidence of PW1 and PW2 tallies with each.

Their evidence clearly shows that when PW2 informed A1 and A2 about his inability to procure the money, the 2nd accused dragged PW1 to the courtyard of the house and threatened her stating that the 1st accused will be married to a more beautiful woman than her's, if the demand is not met.
The first accused also caught hold of her hair and assaulted her.

At that time,
when PW1 demanded back the gold ornaments and money she had given to them, the 1 st accused slapped her on her face and the 2 nd accused punched her on her stomach.
PW2 timely intervened and took PW1 to the hospital, where she was treated for two days.
It is to be seen that even though these witnesses have been cross examined in extenso, no material contradictions have been brought out to disbelieve their testimonies on these aspects.

Further, the evidence of PW5, the doctor coupled with Ext.P4 wound certificate, goes to show that PW1 had approached her seeking medical aid, immediately after the incident at about 5.00 p.m, with an allegation of assault by 2025:KER:72168 her husband and in-laws and with complaints of pain on her head and lower abdomen.
The afore evidence also gives credence and support to the version of PW1 and PW2 regarding the events which transpired on 23.10.2001.

In the light of the afore discussions, I find that both the trial court and the appellate court have not committed any illegality or error in appreciating the evidence on record on this aspect and in reaching a conclusion of guilt against the 1 st and 2nd accused, under Section 498A of IPC.
11.
Now the question to be considered is regarding the sentence.

Considering the nature of the offence, its gravity, the fact that the incident has taken place in the year 2001, the fact that no injuries have been sustained by PW1 and the facts and circumstances of this case, I am of the view that, the sentence imposed on the revision petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 498A of IPC is on a higher side and the same can be modified and reduced to one of simple imprisonment for a period of 15 days.

But I am also of the view that the revision petitioners/ accused Nos. 1 and 2 can be ordered to pay a compensation of Rs. 20,000/- each to PW1 as compensation under Section 357(3) of Cr.P.C and in case of default, to 2025:KER:72168 undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month.
12. In the result, this criminal R.P is allowed in part as follows.

i) The conviction and sentence rendered against the revision petitioners/ accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 406 IPC in CC No. 221/2002 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court I, Parappanangadi and as confirmed in Crl.Appeal No.369/2010 by the Sessions Court, Manjeri are set aside.
